compareCandidate.label: Prey vs. predator
compareCandidate.description: Prey is hunted and eaten; the predator does the hunting. Many animals are both - a mouse is prey to an owl but a predator to an insect.

plainLanguageExplanation: Prey is any animal that predators hunt and eat. Rabbits, mice, deer, and fish are common prey. To survive, prey have their own adaptations: many are fast, some blend into their surroundings with camouflage, some hide in burrows, and many live in groups so there are more eyes watching for danger. Prey and predators are locked in a constant race - as predators get faster, prey get faster too, and this balance keeps both populations healthy. A healthy ecosystem needs both prey and predators.

whyItMatters: Prey are half of the predator-prey race that shapes every ecosystem - their defenses keep them alive, and their numbers keep predators fed. Understanding them shows why prey adaptations are just as important as predator hunting skills.
didYouKnow: A rabbit's eyes sit on the sides of its head, giving it almost a full 360 degrees of vision - perfect for spotting a predator coming from any direction.
